headline: Border Cartographer Resigns After Discovering 'Boundary Line' Is Just A Persistent Coffee Stain On His Drafting Table
body:
The Ministry of External Affairs’ lead senior cartographer, Ramesh Kulkarni, resigned abruptly this morning after realizing that the geopolitical ‘no-go zone’ he has been defending for three decades was actually a dried espresso spill from 1994. Kulkarni, who spent years drafting stern diplomatic responses to territorial encroachment, discovered the error while attempting to clean his workspace during a mandatory office-wide spring cleaning initiative.

“I spent twenty years pointing to that specific brown blotch and calling it a sovereign demarcation line,” said Kulkarni, while packing his compass and protractor into a cardboard box. “I have personally participated in six high-level international summits where I fiercely defended that stain’s historical legitimacy against foreign counterparts. It turns out, I was just defending a Nescafe spill that hardened into a dark, craggy shape resembling a mountain range.”

Junior bureaucrats at the ministry have already begun the painstaking process of explaining the revelation to neighboring delegates, many of whom have built their entire national defense strategies around the location of the coffee-stained border. The office is currently considering replacing the stain with a small piece of scotch tape, though they fear the adhesive might accidentally imply a new maritime trade route.

“We are treating this as a sensitive transition period,” said a department spokesperson, clutching a damp cloth. “Until we can figure out if the stain represents a contested valley or a forgotten snack break, we are advising all border patrol agents to simply stare at the horizon and ignore any questions about topography.”
caption: When your geopolitical career is built on a desk spill. ☕️🗺️ #Diplomacy #BorderControl #OfficeLife #Cartography (satire)
